SPECIFICATION FOR 
AEROSPACE BOLTS AND NUTS ( MJ THREADS ) 

PART 2 DIMENSIONS FOR BOLTS AND NUTS 



1. Scope — In this part, the dimensions for MJ threads for bolts and nuts of nominal diameter range 
from 1 '6 to 39 mm used in aerospace construction are specified. Part 1 of the specification covers 
the basic profile of the threads.

IS : 10980 ( Part 2) -1984 

2 9 4 Provisions for Coated Threads — Before coating, the dimensions of the threads shall be compatible 
with: 

a) the thickness of the coating selected, and 

b) the maximum and minimum dimensions specified in this standard. 

In order to reduce the number of manufacturing and inspection tools, it is recommended that, 
where possible, standardized tolerance classes for threads ( grade and position ) be used. 

3. Profiles 

3.1 The position and forms of the actual profiles indicating maximum, minimum and basic for bolt 
and nut threads are indicated in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2.

4. Threads 

4.1 Bolt Threads — The connection between the root diameter d t and the flanks of the thread is rounded 
in form. This connection shall iie within the following iimits: 

a) d 3t Max and a width of 0*312 5 P (corresponding to the point of tangency between diameter 
cA and the flanks of the thread). This implies a maximum radius equal to 0'180 42 P; and 

b) t/ 3 , Min and a minimum radius equal to 0'150 11 P. 

Within these iimits, any continuous non-reversing biended curve is permitted, provided that ii 
comprises radii not less than 0150 11 P. 

4.2 The form of the connection between the root diameter D% and the thread flanks is not mandatory. 
However, in practice, the root is generally rounded beyond the nominal diameter (d, D). The value 
of the radius is not specified. 



IS : 10980 (Part2)- 1984 



4>D 3 max. 




<$> 1 max. 



FIG. 2 LIMIT PROFILES FOR NUT THREADS 



5. Dimensional Variations 

5.1 Within the limits of the pitch diameter, the sum of the variations on the pitch ( lead ), the flank 
angle and the helix, as well as variations in taper and circularity, and any other variations affecting 
the form of the thread, shall not exceed 0*5 times the tolerance on the pitch diameter. 

6. Designation 

6.1 Threads complying with the requirements of this standard shall be designated by: 

a) a letter identifying metric threads: M; 

b) a letter symbolizing the thread profile: J; 

c) the nominal diameter xthe pitch: in millimetres; and 

d) the tolerance class on pitch diameter, and the tolerance class on the major diameter for bolts 
or on the minor diameter for nuts. 



Examples: 

A bolt with metric thread and J profile, of nominal diameter 6 mm, and pitch 1 mm, and 
tolerance class 4h6h would be designated MJ 6 x 1 - 4h6h. 

A nut with metric thread and J profile, of nominal diameter 6 mm, and pitch 1 mm, and 
tolerance class 4H5H would be designated MJ 6 x 1 - 4H5H.
